# Single-operator panel

The private `/admin` workspace provides users, access overrides, suspension,
read-only quota reporting, an immutable audit history, and the global sending
switch. It provides no impersonation, mailbox access, or billing-provider writes.
Dodo remains test-mode only.

## Deployment and recovery

1. Drain account-deletion workers. Older workers delete audit records and will
   fail after the new immutable-audit migration.
2. Apply migrations with `npm run db:deploy`; deploy this application and its
   updated workers together before resuming deletion work.
3. Set a new `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` with the same database as `DATABASE_URL`, a
   **different, fresh login**, and a randomly generated password of at least
   24 characters. Never reuse the application owner connection. Run
   `npx tsx scripts/provision-admin-db.ts` explicitly using owner credentials.
   It creates the login and grants only enumerated columns and operations; it
   refuses an existing role rather than inheriting unknown grants. It prints
   only fixed result codes. Keep both URLs server-side and out of shell history.
4. Run the disposable test harness and verify forbidden-column access before
   provisioning the operator. `npm run test:usage:db -- --e2e --browser=admin,dodo-billing,feature-gates`
   creates its own temporary restricted credentials. PostgreSQL runs in Docker;
   Next.js runs on the host. No real provider calls occur in these tests.
5. Promote an existing account with its UUID and expected Google subject:
   `npx tsx scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts promote USER_UUID EXPECTED_GOOGLE_SUBJECT`.
   Use a trusted terminal; the subject is an identity identifier. The script
   serializes provisioning, refuses a second operator, and atomically audits
   promotion. Never bootstrap by email or by changing a role through the UI.
6. Configure the additional Google OAuth callback URI
   `https://YOUR_HOST/api/auth/callback/google-admin` (use the local origin in
   development). The normal Gmail callback remains `/api/auth/callback/google`.
7. Visit `/admin`, use **Verify Google identity**, and manually verify that a
   signed Google ID token supplies fresh `auth_time`. Mutation access fails
   closed if Google omits it. Mocked tests cannot certify Google's behavior.

Use an operator Google account protected by a passkey/security key and MFA;
restrict access to database owner credentials, the host, backups, and OAuth
configuration. Do not share operator sessions. Session refresh never renews the
15-minute mutation window. The identity-only provider requests `openid email
profile`, uses state/PKCE/nonce, binds the result to the existing session and a
five-minute encrypted challenge, verifies the ID token signature and Google
subject, and neither creates users nor updates Gmail credentials. Freshness
comes only from signed `auth_time`, never `iat`. See Google's
[OIDC claim reference](https://developers.google.com/identity/openid-connect/reference).

For recovery or rollback, revoke offline:
`npx tsx scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts revoke USER_UUID EXPECTED_GOOGLE_SUBJECT`.
Revocation is audited and effective on the next guarded request, including
already-issued sessions. Keep the migration, audit events, usage evidence,
cancellations, and sending-switch state. Deploy a fix rather than reversing the
migration or resetting quotas. Restore role credentials by provisioning another
fresh login and replacing `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`, then remove obsolete grants
through the database operator's normal credential-rotation process.

## Behavior

- Every admin page, query, and action checks current role, suspension, and pending
  deletion through the restricted login. Mutations lock and recheck the actor.
  There is no fallback connection when admin configuration is missing.
- Reports use one repeatable-read, read-only transaction. Explicit DTOs exclude
  credentials, Google subjects, message content, contact data, resume paths,
  provider IDs, and arbitrary reasons. Legacy audit JSON is never returned.
- Usage is reconstructed from content-free ledger/import evidence, with the
  ledger's direct-assignment, overlapping-period, and deduplication rules.
  Confirmed/imported sends and reserved/attempting/uncertain consumption are
  separate. Remaining allowance never goes negative. Unresolved billing or
  unverified accounting displays unknown usage rather than fresh credit.
  Pending uncharged reservations remain conservatively reserved when normal
  lifecycle processing has not yet rebound them after an override boundary.
- Search is case-insensitive, bounded to 160 characters. Effective-plan filters
  run before the 50-row `(createdAt,id)` cursor. Applying filters drops cursors.
- All mutations require predefined reasons and a stable UUID request ID.
  Identical successful retries return the original safe acknowledgement;
  conflicting reuse is rejected. A maximum of 10 new successful mutations per
  operator per minute uses the durable billing-rate-limit table. Failed writes
  roll back both state, audit, and rate-limit consumption.
- Overrides expire after 30 days by default. A Free override requires explicit
  acknowledgement that billing continues. Overrides never change provider
  state or clear usage. Mutations re-evaluate accounting buckets under owner
  locks without reading campaign content. Existing worker/lifecycle checks
  enforce eligibility and rebind queued work before a new claim.
- Suspension cancels READY unattempted work and releases only proven
  unsubmitted reservations. It preserves attempted/uncertain evidence, existing
  resumes, billing cancellation, account export/deletion, and support. It cannot
  target the current operator. Unsuspension does not restart work or reconnect
  Gmail. Previously issued Blob tokens may upload until expiry; activation is
  denied and completion cleans up unactivated files.
- Global-control updates conflict with the shared lock held by final claims.
  After a disable commits, subsequent claims see disabled controls. A claim
  committed earlier cannot be recalled; no database lock spans a Gmail call.
- Audit UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE is blocked, even for the application connection.
  Only FK-triggered nulling on user removal is allowed. Immutable UUID snapshots
  and event data survive account deletion. New events have action-specific
  schemas, fixed reason codes, and a normalized request hash.
- `lastActiveAt` records visible application navigation through an authenticated
  same-origin endpoint, at most once every 15 minutes. Polling, workers, and
  admin inspection do not mark another user's activity. Missing history is
  shown as “Unknown.”
